about: Drafted clinical questions awaiting relevance judgments.
These have NO grades. Adding them would repeat the problem the existing
judgment set already has — one non-clinician's reading standing in for a
clinical one — at seven times the scale. They are questions only.
TO LABEL THEM:
uv run python -m brahmo.ir.worksheet          # writes a labelling sheet
Judge only the pooled candidates the worksheet lists, not all 29 guidelines.
Pooling is how TREC collections are built; its known bias is that a
document no retriever surfaced is never judged, so recall is optimistic.
With 29 documents and four retrievers the pools are close to exhaustive,
which is the one advantage of a corpus this small.
WHY THESE QUESTIONS:
Each carries a `probes` field naming the retrieval failure it is designed
to expose. A set made only of questions whose words appear in their answer
measures nothing except lexical overlap, and would make BM25 look better
than it is. The categories:
lexical        the question's terms appear in the answer. The easy case,
included so the hard ones have something to contrast with.
vocabulary-gap the answer uses different words than the question. This is
where BM25's 0.683 recall ceiling comes from.
distractor     an obvious keyword points at the wrong guideline.
cost           affordability, NLEM, Jan Aushadhi. Often phrased with no
clinical vocabulary at all.
multi-hop      needs two guidelines combined; neither alone answers it.
negative       nothing in the corpus answers it. A retriever that returns
something confident here is worse than one returning
nothing, and no metric sees that unless such queries exist.
Negative controls should be graded with NO relevant documents. The harness
skips them when scoring ranked metrics; they are there so a precision or
abstention measure can be added later without rebuilding the set.

questions.question: He's on Metformin 2g and otherwise well. What HbA1c should I actually be targeting for a 48-year-old with no complications?
He had a rash on cotrimoxazole years ago. Does that put sulfonylureas off the table?
He eats two cups of white rice at lunch every day. What do I tell him?
His BP is 134/86 on telmisartan. Does the hypertension change which second agent I add for his diabetes?
How much exercise should I be prescribing alongside the drugs?
Her eGFR is 32. Can she stay on metformin at all, or does it come off now?
She takes pregabalin 75mg BD for her neuropathy. Is there anything about that combination with her diabetes regimen I should know?
If I want a gliptin at this level of renal function, which one avoids dose adjustment?
Her retinopathy is proliferative. Should I worry about correcting an HbA1c of 9.2 too quickly?
Is she still a candidate for an SGLT2 inhibitor at an eGFR of 32, given she also has albuminuria?
She's on aspirin 75mg. With an eGFR of 32 and no prior cardiac event, is that still appropriate?
He drives an auto-rickshaw twelve hours a day. Which agents are unsafe for someone doing that?
What is the cheapest regimen that will actually bring an HbA1c of 8.8 down? He earns about 800 rupees a day.
He has fatty liver on ultrasound and an ALT of 68. Does that steer the drug choice?
Before I commit him to lifelong therapy, does he need a second confirmatory test?
What would a month actually cost him if he buys from a Jan Aushadhi Kendra instead of a retail chemist?
Nearest cath lab is 150 minutes away by road. What do I do here, now?
Streptokinase or tenecteplase — how do I decide between them for this man?
He's ESI-covered. Does that change which thrombolytic I reach for?
He had anaphylaxis to penicillin in 2020. Can I still give heparin and a P2Y12 inhibitor?
How long does he stay on dual antiplatelet therapy after this admission?
What ECG criteria am I actually applying to call this an anterior STEMI rather than early repolarisation?
He's on aspirin and ticagrelor three months post-stent and now has AF. How long do I keep all three drugs running?
Should I step him down from ticagrelor to clopidogrel now that he needs an anticoagulant as well?
His CHA2DS2-VASc is 3 and he's male. Is anticoagulation optional at that score or indicated?
Which DOAC would you pick, and is it something CGHS will reimburse?
He's 66 with established coronary disease. Should I be relaxing his glycaemic target?
Her potassium is 5.1 on ramipril plus spironolactone. Do I hold either of them?
With an ejection fraction of 30%, which diabetes drugs are outright contraindicated?
Can she have an SGLT2 inhibitor when she has both heart failure and CKD 3a, or does one rule it out?
She's been on glimepiride for years. Is that a problem now that her heart failure is established?
If I add an SGLT2 inhibitor, how often should I be rechecking her potassium?
Her BNP came back at 850. Does that number change anything about how I manage her diabetes?
She has moderate rheumatic mitral stenosis with AF. Apixaban or warfarin?
Her CHA2DS2-VASc works out to 2. Does that score decide the anticoagulation question here?
Newly diagnosed diabetes on top of established rheumatic heart disease. Where do I start her?
What INR range am I aiming for once she's established on warfarin?
She's 12 weeks pregnant and on metformin. Do I continue it or move her to insulin?
What HbA1c target applies in the first trimester?
Which of the drugs she's currently on are teratogenic and need stopping today?
Acute STEMI and an aspirin allergy on file. What's my antiplatelet strategy?
His glucose is 340 with no prior diabetes history. Do I treat this as new diabetes or as a stress response?
He has no insurance and no savings. Which reperfusion option can he actually afford?
Does the hyperglycaemia change the reperfusion decision at all, or do I treat the STEMI exactly as I would otherwise?
